## How the guide defines it

Not addressed in guide.

## How the guide uses it

On 16 pages, and always attached to a specific game rather than stated as a system. Dustin Swedelson identifies Arkansas hosting Tulsa on September 26 as a dreaded lookahead spot with Texas A&M the following week; Aaron Moore builds a Clemson bet on a mid-September flight to Berkeley sitting between two heavyweight home games and three of the last four on the road. Sacramento State's Under cites midweek games and Midwest travel as practical burdens of the MAC move.

## Working definition — TTW DERIVED

Betting angles arising from a game's context rather than the teams' quality — rest, short weeks, lookahead and letdown spots, travel, and scheduling sequence.

## Why it matters — TTW DERIVED

It is the main way the guide reasons about *when* a game is played rather than *who* is playing, and it is how a schedule argument gets from a strength-of-schedule rank down to individual weeks.

## How bettors use it in this guide

Named and argued in prose, one game at a time. The guide prints no situational database, no rest-differential column and no historical hit rate for any of these spots.
